# EventChip

An upcoming event as a small chip that leads to it: how soon it starts, its title cut to one line, and where the person stands with it after a dot ("Needs you"). Starting soon or happening now draws its border and time in the primary color. It is a `Badge`, so `onClick` makes it a button and `href` a link (without either it is a static label), with Badge's touch target and press feedback, and screen readers hear its `label`, time, title and status in order. Pass `<RelativeTime>` as `when` to keep the time current.

```tsx
import { EventChip } from "@/registry/ouro/components/ouro/event-chip/event-chip";
```

## Example

```tsx
<EventChip label="Next meeting" when="in 12 min" title="Weekly sync" state="soon" status="Needs you" statusTone="warning" onClick={openBriefing} />
```

## Use instead when

- Use `MeetingRow` instead for the event in a list, and `Badge` for a label that is not an event.

## Props

Type: `EventChipProps`.

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `className` | `string` |  | Layout only: margins, a maximum width (`max-w-80`). Appearance classes warn in development. |
| `href` | `string` |  | Makes the chip a link to the event, as Badge's `href`. |
| `label` | `string` |  | What the chip is, read first by screen readers ("Next meeting"). |
| `onClick` | `MouseEventHandler<HTMLElement>` |  | Makes the chip a button, such as one that opens the event's briefing. |
| `ref` | `Ref<HTMLElement>` |  | Reaches the rendered element. |
| `state` | `"now" \| "upcoming" \| "soon"` | `"upcoming"` | `soon` and `now` draw the chip's border and time in the primary color. |
| `status` | `string` |  | Where the person stands with it, as a short label after a dot ("Ready", "Needs you"). |
| `statusTone` | `"primary" \| "secondary" \| "destructive" \| "success" \| "warning"` | `"secondary"` | The status dot's color role from the theme, named after its token. |
| `title` (required) | `string` |  | The event's title, cut to one line ("Weekly sync"). |
| `when` (required) | `ReactNode` |  | When, already formatted ("in 12 min", "Tomorrow 9:00"); pass `<RelativeTime>` for one that keeps itself current. |

## Don't use

These are not props. Passing one fails the type check with the fix in the error, and in development a console message names the fix.

- `onOpen`: Not a prop. The chip opens through `onClick` or `href`: `<EventChip onClick={open}>`.
- `soon`: Not a prop. How near it is, is `state`: `<EventChip state="soon">`.
- `subject`: Not a prop. The event's title is `title`: `<EventChip title="Weekly sync">`.

## `className` is for layout only

Pass margins, width and grid placement (`mt-4`, `w-full`, `col-span-2`). Your classes always win over Ouro UI's: EventChip merges `className` last with `cn` (tailwind-merge), so a class that conflicts with its own replaces it.[^layout-classes]

Appearance comes from props, not classes. In development, a class that sets appearance logs one warning per component instance, naming the prop to use instead. A class sets appearance when, after its variants (`hover:`, `sm:`) and any `!` are removed, it starts with `bg-`, `text-`, `border-`, `rounded-`, `shadow-`, `font-`, `ring-`, `from-`, `via-`, `to-`, `fill-` or `stroke-`, or is `border`, `rounded`, `shadow` or `ring`, or has a `dark:` variant. Text wrapping, overflow and table layout classes (`text-wrap`, `text-ellipsis`, `border-collapse`) are layout and do not warn.

Alignment classes (`text-center`) warn too: set alignment on a parent element.
